### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.operators

### Question

I noticed that `gx` is mapped by default in Neovim to open URIs or files under the cursor (e.g., with a web browser or file explorer). Since I want to preserve this default behavior for `gx`, I attempted to remap the `mini.operators` exchange prefix from `gx` to `gX`.  

Here’s the configuration I tried:
```lua
MiniOperators.setup({
    exchange = {
        prefix = "gX", -- or `gl`
    },
})
```
However, after setting this up, `gx` still seems to be affected by `mini.operators`, preventing the default URI-opening functionality from working. How can I properly remap `mini.operators` to use `gX` and ensure `gx` retains its default behavior in Neovim?

as you can see in this picture:  
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b42cdc5-d95c-4f0a-87d4-85b9f9251172)

This prevents me from using `gx` to open links or files.

comment_data.body:
That's strange. 

Your setup is working for me.

Do you have a duplicate setup? I can reproduce having both `gx` and `gX` for `exchange` like so:

```lua
require("mini.operators").setup()
require("mini.operators").setup({
  exchange = { prefix = "gX" },
})
```

EDIT:

The init.lua below is also working:

<details>

<summary>init.lua</summary>

```lua
---@diagnostic disable: undefined-global
local function setup_deps(path_to_site)
  local mini_path = path_to_site .. "pack/deps/start/mini.nvim"
  if not vim.uv.fs_stat(mini_path) then
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    vim.fn.system({ "git", "clone", "--filter=blob:none", "https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim", mini_path })
    vim.cmd("packadd mini.nvim | helptags ALL")
    vim.cmd('echo "Installed `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
  end
  require("mini.deps").setup({ path = { package = path_to_site } })
end
setup_deps(vim.fn.stdpath("data") .. "/site/")

vim.g.mapleader = " "
MiniDeps.now(function() require("mini.operators").setup({ exchange = { prefix = "gX" } }) end)


```

</details>

The output of commands `:map gx` and `:map gX` is correct.

reply_data.body:
Yes, everything works here as expected and is probably the result of several `setup()` calls.

@krovuxdev, the shear fact that you use `MiniOperators.setup` (instead of `require('mini.operators').setup`) and it works, means that there was a `require('mini.operators').setup()` call before it. The `MiniOperators` global table is created only inside that call. Remove that prior call and use `require('mini.operators').setup()` here.

---

That said, I'd suggest the other way around and map `gX` to open URI under cursor (prior to calling `require('mini.operators').setup`). Here is [how I do it](https://github.com/echasnovski/nvim/blob/3b97b4bf2cce4ea9d8f0cdb539d98118dfa35406/plugin/20_mini.lua#L323-L330). That said, I think this should be done by 'mini.operators' itself (same as it clears up `gr*` built-in mappings for `gr`)... :thinking:

reply_data.body:
> I wonder why the other mini modules work using `MiniPick.setup`, changing keymaps without duplicating anything 🤔. Could you explain why `operators` behaves differently? (just out of curiosity)

The 'mini.operators' module, as well as *many* others (like 'mini.operators', 'mini.surround', 'mini.ai', 'mini.move', 'miin.splitjoin', 'mini.completion', 'mini.diff', etc.) creates global mappings inside its `setup()` call.

Only some modules don't create global mappings. Instead they create buffer-local (like 'mini.files'), temporary (like `jump_next`, `jump_prev`, `stop` in 'mini.snippets'; but not `expand`), or not "true" mappings at all (like 'mini.pick').
